title: `PATH=/bin:/us<TAB>` then ctrl-n: zsh leaves `PATH=/bin:/usr`, zshrs leaves `PATH=/bin:/usr/` — the menu's next match arrives with a trailing slash

observed.cursor: zsh row 0 col 19, zshrs row 0 col 20
observed.notes: The TAB alone agrees — that is control0, and it is what makes ctrl-n the variable: the divergence is introduced by the menu's next-match insertion, not by the completion that populated the menu. The colon is not required either: `PATH=/us` with the same keys diverges the same way (variant0, its own fingerprint 5279658858). What IS required is that the parameter is PATH: `ZZ=/bin:/us` with the same keys agrees (control1). A third control measured in round 6 and not pinned here because it costs 44s to replay — `ls /bin:/us` with the same keys — also agrees, so it is the assignment to a colon-path parameter that carries the defect, not the word shape.
